title: Activation-aware INT8 quant pipeline and calibration harness for SmoothQuant workflows
creator: Aisha Ramanujan
description:
Goal: Implement an activation-aware INT8 quantization pipeline (SmoothQuant-compatible) end-to-end: calibration data selection, per-layer activation rescaling, per-channel weight quantization, calibration metrics, automated profile generation (quant-profiles), and runtime kernel hooks to select the appropriate execution path. Deliverables include a calibration CLI, a reproducible validation suite vs FP32 baselines, model artifact format for quant profiles, and runtime kernel integration that supports fast fallback and feature flags.

Scope & constraints:
- Support encoder-decoder and decoder-only Transformer blocks used in Redwood model catalog, focusing on MatMul-heavy attention and feed-forward layers.
- Produce INT8 profiles that capture per-tensor activation scales and optional per-channel weight scales; support symmetric and asymmetric quantization modes.
- Ensure SmoothQuant-style activation-weight balancing: compute layer-wise scaling factors and store as quant profile entries so inference runtime can apply activation rescaling on-the-fly.
- Calibration must be stable under small representative datasets (1k-5k examples) and produce metrics (KL divergence, MSE, max-error) per-layer.
- Integrate with runtime kernel selection so kernels can opt-in for INT8 fast paths or fall back to FP16/FP32 when accuracy regressions exceed thresholds.

Implementation checklist:
- Calibration harness: CLI that accepts model, dataset, sampling strategy, num-batches, and outputs a JSON quant profile (activation_scales, weight_scales, layer_map, quant_mode). Also emit a per-layer metrics report and histogram artifacts.
- Representative dataset: build standard Redwood calibration sets for language modeling (Wiki + internal snippets) and NLU downstream tasks; include a sampling config to mimic request token length distribution.
- Quant profile format: simple JSON with top-level lists; keys are layer names. Avoid nested objects; store numbers and lists only. Add versioning field.
- SmoothQuant balancing: implement stable solver for activation shift factors using per-layer statistics. Add optional bias-correction pass for first-order correction.
- Validation suite: automated run that measures perplexity on held-out LM set, zero-shot via eval harness, and a small downstream QA/NLI subset. Define regression thresholds (perplexity +2% absolute or task F1 -1.5 points as failure).
- Runtime integration: add kernel selection hook that reads quant profile and applies activation rescaling in the JIT path before MatMul. Implement two kernel paths: quant-fast (INT8 with activation rescale + per-channel weight dequant on the fly) and compatibility path (FP16).
- Tests and CI: unit tests for profile parsing, deterministic calibration on fixed RNG seeds, and integration tests with the runtime using a small distilled model. Add performance microbenchmarks for latency and throughput.
- Rollout plan: start behind the feature flag experimental/quant-int8-smooth, run canary against dedicated infra with traffic mirroring, collect accuracy and perf metrics for 2 weeks, then enable for more models by whitelist.

Risks and mitigations:
- Outliers in activation histograms cause large scale factors: add percentile clipping and outlier rejection heuristics.
- Calibration dataset mismatch with production payloads: provide a sampling policy and allow customers to supply representative traces for private deployments.
- Runtime numerical instability: implement fallback thresholds in kernel that detect re-scaling overflow/underflow and fallback to FP16 for the affected layer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration CLI produces quant profiles that reproduce FP32 perplexity within +2% on the LM validation set for at least 3 out of 4 test models.
- Runtime kernel INT8 fast path shows >=1.8x per-token throughput improvement vs FP16 on p4d-like hardware and end-to-end latency degradation <15% p95.
- CI includes deterministic unit tests and an integration smoke test validating correctness of activation rescale behavior.
- Documentation: design doc and example notebook for generating quant profiles and deploying them to a dedicated instance.

If any accuracy regressions appear during canary, the runtime must support automated rollback to FP16 for the impacted model and region.
